label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea.
unit: Anne Shirley arrived at Green Gables in Avonlea as a fiery, imaginative eleven-year-old orphan, winning over the hearts of her guardians, Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. She formed a lifelong bond with her bosom friend Diana Barry and excelled academically, winning the Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy. After Matthew's sudden death, she postponed her college studies to stay with Marilla, teaching at Avonlea School and helping organize the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. Later, she attended Redmond College in Kingsport, where she made dear friends like Philippa Gordon and eventually realized her true love was Gilbert Blythe after rejecting Roy Gardner. Following her graduation and a three-year stint as principal of Summerside High School while engaged, Anne married Gilbert in the orchard at Green Gables. The couple moved to Four Winds Light to settle in their 'House of Dreams,' where Anne forged close friendships with Captain Jim, Leslie Moore, and Miss Cornelia Bryant. Though she suffered the tragic loss of her firstborn infant daughter, Joy, Anne recovered her spirit, helped resolve Leslie's life complications, and gave birth to a healthy son, Little Jem.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School
unit: Anthony Pye attends Avonlea School when Anne Shirley begins her tenure as the village schoolmistress. Influenced by his family's prejudices, particularly his uncle Josiah Pye, Anthony acts out and stubbornly disregards Anne's authority, proving to be one of her most challenging students. Anne attempts to win him over with patience and kindness, but her efforts initially fail to break through his sullen defiance. After Anne reaches a breaking point and chastises him severely with a whip for an act of disobedience, Anthony surprisingly changes his attitude, having come to respect her firmness. From that moment onward, he becomes one of Anne's most obedient and devoted pupils, defending her loyalty against criticism from other members of his family.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina enters Anne Shirley's life
unit: Aunt Jamesina enters Anne Shirley's life during Anne's college years at Redmond. When Anne, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon decide to rent Patty's Place in Kingsport, Stella invites her Aunt Jamesina to join them as their chaperone and housekeeper. She brings her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph, and quickly establishes Patty's Place as a cozy, welcoming haven for the students. Throughout their time at Redmond College, she offers gentle wisdom, practical guidance, and lively conversation to the girls and their frequent visitors. After the girls graduate and scatter, she continues to maintain warm feelings and correspondence with them.

label: History
value: Billy grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Billy grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school with Anne Shirley and her peers. As he reached adulthood, he settled into farming at the Andrews home. Anne promptly declined the proposal, much to her own relief and Billy's brief disappointment. Later, Billy married Nettie Blewett, a practical woman suited to his sensible lifestyle.

label: History
value: Captain Jim spent much of his youth at sea.
unit: Captain Jim spent much of his youth and adult life at sea, traveling to distant lands and surviving numerous maritime adventures. After retiring from his life as a sea captain, he took up the position of keeper at the Four Winds Point lighthouse. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe move to their 'house of dreams' nearby, Captain Jim becomes one of their dearest friends and welcomes them warmly. He shares his vast treasury of tales and his cherished life book with Owen Ford, a visiting author, who transforms Captain Jim's life story into a successful novel. Captain Jim lives long enough to see his life's experiences published into a book and to witness the happiness of his dear friends Leslie and Owen. He passes away peacefully at the lighthouse shortly after seeing his dream fulfilled.

label: History
value: Carl Meredith is one of the four children.
unit: Carl Meredith is introduced as one of the four motherless children of the new Glen St. Mary minister, John Meredith. Raised with little discipline due to his father's absent-minded nature, Carl spends much of his time playing in Rainbow Valley with his siblings and the Blythe children. His penchant for collecting bugs, frogs, and snakes repeatedly causes humorous chaos at the manse and during social calls. He joins the Good Samaritan Club formed by the manse children and their friends to help improve their behavior and perform good deeds. Along with his brother Gerald and sisters Jerry and Faith, Carl benefits greatly from the care and guidance of Rosemary West after she marries his father.

unit: Charlotta the Fourth first appears when Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discover Echo Lodge, the secluded home of Miss Lavender Lewis. Having taken over the maid duties at Echo Lodge from her older sisters, Charlotta loyally manages the home and helps keep Miss Lavender's whimsical world running smoothly. She instantly forms a deep admiration for Anne Shirley and plays a helpful role during Stephen Irving's return and his eventual romantic reconciliation with Miss Lavender. Following Miss Lavender's wedding to Stephen Irving, Charlotta moves with them to Boston to continue her service. Years later, when Anne and Gilbert Blythe settle at the House of Dreams in Four Winds, Charlotta travels to assist Anne after the birth of her children, offering her devoted help once again.

value: Miss Cornelia is opininated.
unit: Opininated, sharp-tongued, and fiercely independent, Miss Cornelia is famous for her sweeping disdain for 'men creatures' and Methodists. She is intensely loyal to her friends, practical in all matters, and a indefatigable community gossip with strong Presbyterian convictions.

label: History
value: Miss Cornelia Bryant is a prominent resident of Four Winds Harbor.
unit: Miss Cornelia Bryant is a prominent resident of Four Winds Harbor who warmly welcomes Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe upon their arrival at the house of dreams. She takes an immediate liking to Anne, establishing a close friendship and frequently visiting to share community news and assist with household matters. She acts as a fierce guardian and benefactor to Leslie Moore, aiding her through her difficult life with her brain-injured husband, Dick. Although famous for her vocal contempt for men and marriage, Miss Cornelia shocks the entire community in Anne's House of Dreams by accepting a marriage proposal from her longtime acquaintance, Marshall Elliott, after he finally shaves his beard following a political victory. Following her marriage, she becomes Mrs. Marshall Elliott, though she retains her sharp wit, energetic nature, and strong opinions. By the time of Anne of Ingleside, she remains a devoted friend to the Blythe family and an active figure in Glen St. Mary affairs.

label: History
value: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley
unit: Diana Barry meets Anne Shirley shortly after Anne arrives at Green Gables, and the two young girls swear an oath of everlasting friendship. Early in their acquaintance, Diana accidentally becomes intoxicated on Marilla's raspberry cordial, causing Mrs. Barry to temporarily forbid their friendship until Diana saves her little sister Minnie May from croup. Diana attends Avonlea School and later Queen's Academy alongside Anne, though she opts not to pursue further higher education or a teaching career. She becomes engaged to Fred Wright of Avonlea and marries him, settling down at Orchard Slope. Over the years, she gives birth to children, including her eldest son, Fred Jr., and a daughter named Anne Cordelia. She remains Anne's closest confidante and bosom friend through Anne's teaching years, college life at Redmond, and eventual marriage to Gilbert Blythe.

value: In his youth, Dick was wild.

Following his brain surgery, he regained his true faculties and demonstrated genuine gratitude, remorse, and a desire to make amends for his past behavior.

label: History
value: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds.
unit: Dick Moore grew up at Four Winds and pursued Leslie West, convincing her family to press her into marrying him despite her lack of affection for him. Shortly after their wedding, he left on a trading voyage to the South Seas and failed to return, leaving Leslie trapped in an unhappy marriage to an absent man. Years later, Captain Jim discovered a man in a Cuban asylum matching Dick's description and brought him home to Four Winds. Leslie spent twelve bitter years nursing this brain-damaged, helpless man whom everyone believed to be Dick Moore. When Gilbert Blythe suggested that a trepanning operation might restore the man's memory, Leslie reluctantly agreed. The surgery was successful, but the restored man revealed that he was actually George Moore, Dick's cousin who had joined him on the voyage. George revealed that the real Dick Moore had died of yellow fever in Cuba years earlier, finally freeing Leslie from her burden.

label: History
value: Ellen West lived in the Four Winds region.
unit: Ellen West lived in the Four Winds region and was the youth sweetheart of Captain William MacAllister. Following a foolish quarrel driven by mutual pride, William sailed away on a long voyage without making amends, leaving Ellen heartbroken. Though she refused to marry anyone else, she remained steadfast in her unspoken devotion throughout her life. Decades later, as an elderly woman near death, she was finally reunited in spirit and memory with William's story through Capt'n Jim, learning that William had loved her until his dying day. She passed away shortly after learning the truth, her long grief at last laid to rest.

label: History
value: Faith Meredith moves to Glen St. Mary
unit: Faith Meredith moves to Glen St. Mary when her father, the Reverend John Meredith, accepts the call to the local Presbyterian church. Left largely to themselves due to their father's scholarly absent-mindedness, Faith and her siblings form the Good Conduct Club in the old graveyard to help discipline themselves. She quickly becomes close friends with Anne Blythe's children at Ingleside. Faith's lively escapades, including riding a pig on a dare, often scandalize some of the more conservative members of the Glen congregation. Despite the gossip, her innate warmth and sincerity endear her to her friends and family.

Faith's lively escapades, including riding a pig on a dare, often scandalize some of the more conservative members of the Glen congregation. Despite the gossip, her innate warmth and sincerity endear her to her friends and family.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea School as a teenager.
unit: Gilbert Blythe returned to Avonlea School as a teenager and immediately sparked a multi-year rivalry with Anne Shirley after playfully mocking her red hair. Despite his repeated efforts to apologize and become friends, Anne refused to speak to him for years, driving both of them to excel academically. Their academic rivalry culminated in a tie for the Avery Scholarship at Queen's Academy. After graduation, Gilbert gallantly gave up the Avonlea schoolteaching position to Anne so she could remain at Green Gables after Matthew Cuthbert's death, which finally earned him her friendship. During their time at Redmond College, Gilbert fell deeply in love with Anne and proposed to her, but she initially rejected him, believing she did not love him in that way. Following a near-fatal bout of typhoid fever after college, Gilbert's illness forced Anne to realize her true feelings for him. Once recovered, he proposed again and was accepted. After completing medical school, Gilbert married Anne in the orchard at Green Gables and moved with her to the 'House of Dreams' at Four Winds Harbor to establish his medical practice. In Four Winds, Gilbert earns the respect of the local community, including the cynical Captain Jim and the aloof Leslie Moore. He and Anne face tragic heartbreak when their firstborn child, Joyce, dies shortly after birth, but their marriage endures, and they later welcome a healthy son named Little Jem.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and friend of Anne Shirley, Ruby Gillis, and Diana Barry. Though she lacked Anne's romantic imagination, she joined the girls' childhood 'Story Club,' contributing stories that were noted for being thoroughly practical and sensible. She attended Queen's Academy with Anne and Gilbert Blythe, successfully earning her teacher's certificate in one year. After graduating, she taught school successfully for several years. Jane eventually married a wealthy Winnipeg millionaire, Mr. Winnipeg (Edward Inglis), moving to Western Canada and settling into a prosperous, comfortable married life.

label: History
value: Reverend John Meredith's beloved wife is Cecilia.
unit: Following the death of his beloved wife, Cecilia, Reverend John Meredith accepts the call to become the Presbyterian minister at Glen St. Mary, moving into the manse with his four children—Jerry, Faith, Una, and Thomas Carlyle—and his elderly aunt, Aunt Martha. Devastated by his loss and absorbed in his books, he inadvertently neglects the practical oversight of his household and children. The neglected Meredith children form a close friendship with Anne and Gilbert Blythe's children at Rainbow Valley. After gossip in the village regarding his children's wild antics reaches him, John realizes his shortcomings as a father and strives to pay more attention to their upbringing. Over time, he realizes that his household needs a mother's touch and falls in love with Rosemary West. Although their courtship faces initial obstacles due to a pact between Rosemary and her sister Ellen, the issues are resolved, and John marries Rosemary West.

label: History
value: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Josie Pye grew up in Avonlea as a classmate of Anne Shirley. She frequently antagonized Anne, famously daring her to walk the ridgepole of the Barry kitchen roof, which resulted in Anne breaking her ankle. She attended Queen's Academy to earn her teaching certificate alongside Anne and Gilbert Blythe. After graduating, she taught at various schools on Prince Edward Island. As the years passed, she remained part of the Avonlea social circle, continuing her habit of making malicious and blunt observations about her old classmates, particularly concerning Anne's career and romance with Gilbert.

Anne acts as a catalyst in reuniting Stephen Irving, now a widower, with Miss Lavendar when he returns to Prince Edward Island. Stephen and Miss Lavendar reconcile their past mistakes, marry at Echo Lodge, and move together to Boston, leaving Echo Lodge behind for a happy new life.

label: History
value: Leslie West had a tragic youth in Four Winds.
unit: Leslie West had a tragic youth in Four Winds, losing her family early under devastating circumstances. At sixteen, her mother pressured her into marrying Dick Moore, a crude man who mistreated her before leaving on a sea voyage. Years later, Captain Jim brought back a brain-damaged, amnesiac man from a Cuban hospital whom everyone believed to be Dick, and Leslie spent twelve years selflessly nursing him despite her inner misery. When Anne Shirley and Gilbert Blythe moved to Four Winds, Leslie eventually formed a deep, transformative friendship with Anne. Gilbert later urged the man believed to be Dick to undergo a brain surgery, which revealed his true identity as Dick's cousin, George Moore, meaning Dick had actually died of yellow fever years prior. Freed from her oppressive marriage and her mistaken duty, Leslie embraced a new life, fell in love with Owen Ford, and eventually married him.

label: History
value: James Matthew Blythe is born at Four Winds Point
unit: James Matthew Blythe, known affectionately as Little Jem, is born at Four Winds Point to Anne and Gilbert Blythe, bringing great joy to his parents after the tragic loss of their first child, Joy. During his infancy in Four Winds, he becomes a cherished figure to family friends such as Captain Jim, Miss Cornelia Bryant, and Leslie Moore. When Gilbert's medical practice expands, the Blythe family relocates from the House of Dreams to Ingleside in Glen St. Mary. Growing up at Ingleside, Jem becomes the eldest of an expanding group of Blythe siblings, taking on the role of an older brother to Walter, the twins Anne and Diana, and later Shirley and Rilla. He spends his early childhood playing in nearby natural spots like Rainbow Valley and listening to stories, while forming close bonds with his family and local household figures like Susan Baker.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet life.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived a quiet, unmarried life at Green Gables with her bachelor brother Matthew. Deciding to adopt an orphan boy to help Matthew with farm work, they were mistakenly sent an imaginative girl named Anne Shirley. Though initially determined to return Anne, Marilla quickly relented and agreed to keep and raise her. Over the years, Marilla provided a grounded, disciplined upbringing while gradually warming to Anne's passionate nature and coming to love her deeply. Following Matthew's sudden death, Marilla faced the threat of losing her eyesight and considered selling Green Gables, but Anne decided to stay in Avonlea to support her. Marilla later took in the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith, distant relatives of hers, navigating the challenges of raising the mischievous Davy. As Anne went on to attend college and eventually marry Gilbert Blythe, Marilla remained at Green Gables as a beloved matriarch figure, taking great joy in Anne's visits and new family.

As Anne went on to attend college and eventually marry Gilbert Blythe, Marilla remained at Green Gables as a beloved matriarch figure, taking great joy in Anne's visits and new family.

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott took a solemn vow during a heated political campaign.
unit: Marshall Elliott became a local legend in Four Winds after taking a solemn vow during a heated political campaign twenty years earlier, swearing that he would not cut his hair or shave his beard until the Liberal Party won the election. Because the Conservatives remained in power for two decades, Marshall's hair and beard grew to extraordinary lengths, causing him to avoid social gatherings and live as a recluse. During this time, he maintained a quiet devotion to Miss Cornelia Bryant, who refused to marry him while he looked so wild and persisted in his foolish vow. After the long-awaited Liberal victory finally occurs, Marshall immediately visits the barber, shaves his beard, and cuts his hair, transforming back into a handsome, respectable man. Freshly shaven, he finally marries Miss Cornelia Bryant, settling down to a happy domestic life and becoming a close friend and neighbor to Anne and Gilbert Blythe at the Four Winds Light and later Ingleside.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet life at Green Gables.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lived a quiet life at Green Gables with his unmarried sister Marilla, working their farm in Avonlea. As he grew older and his health began to decline, he and Marilla decided to adopt an orphan boy to help with the farm work. Through a misunderstanding, a young girl named Anne Shirley arrived at the train station instead, but Matthew was instantly captivated by her spirit and convinced Marilla to keep her. Over the following years, Matthew served as Anne's quiet advocate, buying her a puffed-sleeve dress she longed for and constantly encouraging her academic pursuits. His health gradually weakened due to heart trouble, though he remained devoted to Anne as she grew into a young woman and earned her B.A. degree. Matthew passed away suddenly from a heart attack caused by the shock of the Abbey Bank failure, leaving behind a profound legacy of love that shaped Anne's life.

value: Owen Ford arrives at Four Winds Light.
unit: Owen Ford arrives at Four Winds Light seeking a quiet, inspiring location to recover his health and write a novel. While staying near the lighthouse, he becomes acquainted with Anne Shirley Blythe, Gilbert Blythe, Captain Jim Boyd, and Leslie Moore. Upon hearing Captain Jim recount his colorful sea-faring life and lost loves, Owen realizes that Captain Jim's life story is the great novel he himself has been trying to invent. With Captain Jim's permission, Owen transcribes and adapts the captain's 'life book' into a novel entitled 'The Life-Book of Captain Jim.' During his stay, Owen falls deeply in love with Leslie Moore, whose tragic life and beauty captivate him. After Leslie is freed from her tragic situation and her identity crisis is resolved, Owen woos her and eventually proposes. Their collaborative efforts and mutual devotion lead to a happy engagement, and Owen's book becomes a major literary success.

label: History
value: Philippa meets Anne Shirley on the train to Redmond College in Kingsport.
unit: Philippa meets Anne Shirley on the train to Redmond College in Kingsport, and the two quickly become close friends. She joins Anne, Priscilla Grant, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place, where they spend three happy years together during their university studies. Though initially torn between two wealthy hometown suitors, Alec and Alonzo, Philippa eventually meets Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student who wins her heart with his sincerity and character. Overcoming her family's initial disapproval of Jonas's modest prospects, she marries him after graduation. They move to a humble parish in Patterson, where she embraces her new life as a minister's wife with enthusiasm and grace, maintaining a loving, lifelong correspondence with Anne.

label: History
value: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school there.
unit: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school there. He spends much of his time openly courting one of his older students, Prissy Andrews, while neglecting the rest of the classroom. He singles Anne out for severe punishments, such as making her sit with Gilbert Blythe after she arrives late, which prompts Anne to refuse to attend school for months. He also embarrasses Anne by misspelling her name on the blackboard when punishing her for talking. At the end of his term in Avonlea, his departure is met with secret relief by many of the pupils, and he is succeeded by Miss Muriel Stacy.

He singles Anne out for severe punishments, such as making her sit with Gilbert Blythe after she arrives late, which prompts Anne to refuse to attend school for months. He also embarrasses Anne by misspelling her name on the blackboard when punishing her for talking. At the end of his term in Avonlea, his departure is met with secret relief by many of the pupils, and he is succeeded by Miss Muriel Stacy.

label: History
value: Priscilla meets Anne Shirley.
unit: Priscilla first meets Anne Shirley while attending Queen's Academy in Charlottetown, where both study for their teaching certificates. They form a close friendship that continues after graduation while Priscilla takes up a teaching post. When Anne decides to pursue a Bachelor of Arts degree at Redmond College in Kingsport, Priscilla joins her as a fellow classmate. Along with Anne, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard, Priscilla sets up house at Patty's Place, a cozy cottage near the campus that becomes their beloved home during their college years. During her time at Redmond, Priscilla excels academically and shares in the social adventures of their circle. After graduating with her B.A. degree, she travels to Japan to accept a teaching position.

label: History
value: Rachel Lynde was the prominent resident of Avonlea.
unit: Rachel Lynde was the prominent resident of Avonlea who first observed Matthew Cuthbert setting off to fetch an orphan boy, later expressing her horror when Anne Shirley arrived instead. After an initial clash over Anne's temper, Rachel quickly warmed to the young girl and became one of her most loyal advocates and supporters. Over the years, she managed church sewing circles, took a prominent role in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, and offered unsolicited advice to everyone in the neighborhood. Following the death of her meek husband Thomas Lynde, she found herself unable to maintain her farm alone and moved into Green Gables to live with Marilla Cuthbert. Her presence allowed Marilla to keep the property while Anne pursued her career and marriage. Rachel continued to offer matriarchal guidance, support, and friendship to Anne as she moved to Four Winds Light and started her own family.

label: History
value: Bertha Marilla 'Rilla' Blythe is born to Anne and Gilbert Blythe.
unit: Bertha Marilla 'Rilla' Blythe is born to Anne and Gilbert Blythe at Ingleside, completing their family as the youngest of six surviving children. Named after her maternal grandmother Bertha and her mother's benefactor Marilla Cuthbert, she grows up in the warmth and laughter of the Ingleside household. Throughout her early childhood, she is adored and doted on by her parents, her older brothers Jem, Walter, and Shirley, her twin sisters Nan and Di, and the housekeeper Susan Baker. label: History
value: Rosemary West lives at the Beech
unit: Rosemary West lives at the Beech in Glen St. Mary with her older sister, Ellen West. When the widowed minister, John Meredith, moves to the Glen with his unruly children, Rosemary forms a warm bond with the family, particularly with young Walter Blythe and the Meredith children who frequently visit Rainbow Valley. John Meredith falls in love with Rosemary and proposes to her, but she initially declines because of a pact made with Ellen that neither sister would ever marry and leave the other. Anne Blythe and the children are deeply saddened by this refusal, as they recognize Rosemary's potential to bring warmth and order to the manse. Later, Norman Douglas courts Ellen West, which eventually leads Ellen to release Rosemary from her promise. Free to follow her heart, Rosemary accepts John Meredith's proposal and marries him, becoming a devoted stepmother to his four children.

label: History
value: Roy meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College.
unit: Roy meets Anne Shirley at Redmond College when he shares an umbrella with her during a sudden downpour, an encounter that fulfills Anne's lifelong romantic fantasy. He courts her intently throughout their college years, sending her beautiful flowers, writing poetry, and escorting her to social events. Anne accepts his attentions and believes she is in love with him because he matches her imagined ideal of a romantic hero. However, when Roy finally proposes to her in a carefully staged setting, Anne realizes that she does not truly love him and declines his proposal. Devastated and humiliated by her refusal, Roy departs, and the courtship ends permanently.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grows up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby Gillis grows up in Avonlea as one of Anne Shirley's schoolmates and early friends, joining the Story Club and attending Queen's Academy to become a teacher. Throughout her adolescence and early adulthood, she is famous for her numerous suitors and constant romantic chatter. After teaching at various schools, she returns home to Avonlea when her health begins to fail due to consumption (tuberculosis). During her final summer, she spends much time with Anne, confessing her intense terror of dying young and losing the world she loves so much. Through Anne's gentle companionship, Ruby finds spiritual solace and dies peacefully in her sleep, leaving behind a legacy as the fair girl who loved life.

Throughout her adolescence and early adulthood, she is famous for her numerous suitors and constant romantic chatter. After teaching at various schools, she returns home to Avonlea when her health begins to fail due to consumption (tuberculosis). During her final summer, she spends much time with Anne, confessing her intense terror of dying young and losing the world she loves so much. Through Anne's gentle companionship, Ruby finds spiritual solace and dies peacefully in her sleep, leaving behind a legacy as the fair girl who loved life.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy arrives in Avonlea
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy arrives in Avonlea to take over the local school, succeeding the unpopular Mr. Phillips. She quickly revolutionizes the schoolroom by introducing physical culture exercises, nature walks, and creative composition subjects. Recognizing the intellectual promise in Anne Shirley and a group of older students, she organizes a special entrance class to prepare them for the Queen's Academy examinations. Under her guidance and encouragement, her students successfully pass the exams, with Anne tying for first place in the province. Miss Stacy eventually leaves Avonlea to accept a teaching position elsewhere, but she leaves a lasting impression on Anne and the community.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard meets Anne Shirley
unit: Stella Maynard first meets Anne Shirley during their studies at Queen's Academy in Charlottetown. After teaching for a period, she decides to pursue her Bachelor of Arts degree at Redmond College in Kingsport, joining Anne, Priscilla Grant, and later Philippa Gordon. Stella is the primary instigator behind renting Patty's Place, a charming cottage near campus, so that the girls can live together comfortably instead of residing in dreary boarding houses. To manage the household, Stella brings along her family's devoted old housekeeper, Aunt Atossa (Aunt Jamesina), whose presence completes their cozy domestic circle. Stella spends three delightful, memorable years living at Patty's Place with her friends until their graduation from Redmond.

Stella is the primary instigator behind renting Patty's Place, a charming cottage near campus, so that the girls can live together comfortably instead of residing in dreary boarding houses. To manage the household, Stella brings along her family's devoted old housekeeper, Aunt Atossa (Aunt Jamesina), whose presence completes their cozy domestic circle. Stella spends three delightful, memorable years living at Patty's Place with her friends until their graduation from Redmond.

label: History
value: Susan Baker enters the service of Dr. Gilbert Blythe
unit: Susan Baker enters the service of Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at the House of Dreams in Four Winds Port. She quickly proves herself indispensable through her culinary talents, industrious nature, and total devotion to Anne, especially during the tragic loss of Anne's firstborn child, Joy, and the birth of Little Jem. When the family relocates to the larger home of Ingleside in Glen St. Mary, Susan moves with them and continues her role as the heart of the household's domestic operations. Over the years, she helps care for all the Blythe children—Jem, Walter, Nan, Di, Shirley, and Rilla—treating them with the utmost love and protection. She becomes a central, permanent member of the Ingleside family circle, fiercely defending the household against unpleasant guests like Aunt Mary Maria.

label: History
value: Una grows up at the Glen St. Mary manse
unit: Una grows up at the Glen St. Mary manse as the daughter of the dreamy Presbyterian minister, John Meredith. Following her mother's death, she and her siblings are left largely to themselves under the lax care of Aunt Martha, leading to frequent misunderstandings with the town parishioners. Una forms a close bond with the Blythe children, frequently playing with them in Rainbow Valley. She takes on domestic responsibilities beyond her years, worrying constantly about the household's shortcomings. When her father falls in love with Rosemary West, Una overcomes her own fears of losing his affection and plays a crucial role in bringing about their marriage by persuading Rosemary to accept him.

He also formed a special bond with mystical elements of nature, often sensing a strange, distant 'Piping Piper' calling to him in dreams. When he suffered a severe illness, his family feared for his life, but he eventually recovered to continue his literary pursuits.
